_about: ArchiMate 3.1 element classification lookup — distilled from the Framework Cheat Sheet (references/archimate-3.1-cheatsheet.pdf) and the ArchiMate 3.1 specification. Single source of truth for the engine (layer/aspect/fill/annotation) and for agents doing functional decomposition. aspect: active = who/what does it (incl. interfaces = external access points); behaviour = what is done (services = external offers, processes/functions/interactions = internal, events); passive = what is acted upon.

aspects.active: Active structure — entities capable of performing behaviour. Internal: actor, role, collaboration, component, node, device, system software. External (the access points): INTERFACES — every place a service is made available to a consumer.
aspects.behaviour: Behaviour — units of activity. External: SERVICES (what is offered, named as an outcome for the consumer). Internal: PROCESSES (sequenced, end-to-end), FUNCTIONS (grouped by skill/resource, the decomposition unit), INTERACTIONS (performed by a collaboration). EVENTS start/interrupt behaviour.
aspects.passive: Passive structure — objects on which behaviour is performed: business objects, contracts, representations, products; data objects; artifacts, materials.

decomposition_rules: Every SERVICE consumed from outside its realizing element is exposed through an INTERFACE assigned to it: BusinessInterface = a CHANNEL (web portal, phone line, chat, counter); ApplicationInterface = an API/UI/protocol endpoint; TechnologyInterface = a network/infrastructure access point (port, protocol).
Interfaces are ACTIVE structure, never behaviour: an 'API' is an ApplicationInterface, the thing it lets you do is an ApplicationService, the internal work is an ApplicationFunction.

FUNCTION vs PROCESS vs SERVICE: function = capability-like grouping of work inside one component/role (verb+object: 'Route Model Requests'); process = ordered sequence across steps with a trigger and result; service = the externally visible outcome offered to a consumer (noun phrase: 'Model Routing').
Component/Actor/Role/Node ASSIGNED to the behaviour it performs; behaviour REALIZES the service it delivers; interface ASSIGNED to the service it exposes and COMPOSED by the element that owns it.

Business channels sit in the business layer (BusinessInterface) even when implemented by software; the software endpoint that implements the channel is an ApplicationInterface that REALIZES the business interface.

Stakeholder.definition: Individual, team or organisation with interests in the architecture outcome.

Driver.definition: External or internal condition that motivates change.

Assessment.definition: Result of analysing a driver (SWOT-style finding).

Goal.definition: High-level statement of intent or desired end state.

Outcome.definition: Measurable end result that has been achieved.
examples: Two pilots live with per-process spend rollups

Principle.definition: General property that applies to any system in a context — a normative statement.

Requirement.definition: Statement of need a system must realize.

Constraint.definition: Limitation on how the system is realized.

Meaning.definition: Knowledge or expertise present in a concept in a context.

Value.definition: Relative worth of a concept to a stakeholder.

Resource.definition: Asset owned or controlled by an organisation.

Capability.definition: Ability an active structure element possesses; what the organisation can do.

CourseOfAction.definition: Approach or plan to configure capabilities/resources toward goals.

ValueStream.definition: Sequence of value-adding activities producing an overall result.

BusinessActor.definition: Organisational entity capable of performing behaviour.

BusinessRole.definition: Responsibility for performing specific behaviour, to which an actor is assigned.

BusinessCollaboration.definition: Aggregate of two or more roles working together.

BusinessInterface.definition: CHANNEL: point of access where a business service is made available to the environment.
BusinessInterface.confusable_with: ApplicationInterface (the software endpoint that implements the channel)

BusinessProcess.definition: Sequence of behaviours achieving a specific result (has a trigger and an outcome).

BusinessFunction.definition: Collection of behaviour based on chosen criteria (skills, resources), typically stable.

BusinessInteraction.definition: Behaviour performed by a collaboration of two or more roles.

BusinessEvent.definition: Organisational state change that triggers or results from behaviour.

BusinessService.definition: Explicitly defined behaviour exposed to the environment, named as the consumer's outcome.

BusinessObject.definition: Concept used within a business domain.

Contract.definition: Formal specification of agreement between parties.

Representation.definition: Perceptible form of a business object.

Product.definition: Coherent collection of services and objects offered as a whole.

ApplicationComponent.definition: Encapsulation of application functionality; deployable unit.

ApplicationInterface.definition: API / UI / protocol endpoint: point of access where an application service is made available.
ApplicationInterface.confusable_with: ApplicationService (what the endpoint offers) and ApplicationFunction (the internal work)

ApplicationFunction.definition: Automated behaviour performed by a component — the functional decomposition unit (verb + object).
ApplicationFunction.confusable_with: ApplicationService (external outcome) — a function is internal

ApplicationInteraction.definition: Behaviour performed by an application collaboration.

ApplicationProcess.definition: Sequence of application behaviours achieving a result.

ApplicationEvent.definition: Application state change that triggers behaviour.

ApplicationService.definition: Explicitly defined application behaviour exposed to consumers (noun phrase for an outcome).

Node.definition: Computational or physical resource hosting/executing other technology elements.

Device.definition: Physical IT resource with processing capability.

SystemSoftware.definition: Software environment for specific types of components/objects deployed on it.

TechnologyInterface.definition: Network/infrastructure access point where a technology service is made available (port, protocol).

Path.definition: Link between nodes through which they exchange information.

CommunicationNetwork.definition: Set of structures connecting nodes for transmission.

TechnologyFunction.definition: Collection of technology behaviour performed by a node.

TechnologyProcess.definition: Sequence of technology behaviours achieving a result.

TechnologyInteraction.definition: Behaviour performed by a technology collaboration.

TechnologyEvent.definition: Technology state change that triggers behaviour.

TechnologyService.definition: Explicitly defined technology behaviour exposed to its environment.

Artifact.definition: Piece of data used or produced in development/deployment/operation.

Equipment.definition: Machines/tools that create, use, store, move or transform materials.

DistributionNetwork.definition: Physical network for transporting materials or energy.

WorkPackage.definition: Series of actions to achieve results within time/resource constraints.

Deliverable.definition: Precisely defined result of a work package.

Plateau.definition: Relatively stable architecture state for a period of time.

Location.definition: Place or position where elements are located.

Grouping.definition: Aggregates elements that belong together by some criterion.

Junction.definition: Connects relationships of the same type (and/or).
